turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Good morning, thanks for calling Acme Life, you're speaking with Mia. Just so you know, this call is recorded for quality and training purposes. How can I help you today?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Oh, morning Mia. I saw your ad in the paper on the weekend, the life cover one, and thought I'd give you a ring and find out a bit more.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Of course, happy to help. Before we get into your details or any quotes, could I please confirm your full name and date of birth?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yep, it's Liam Patrick O'Brien. Date of birth is the 14th of March, 1959.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thanks, Liam. That's all confirmed. Before I tell you about the cover itself, do you mind if I ask a little about your situation and what's got you thinking about life insurance?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No, not at all. I've just retired, actually. Taught primary school for thirty-odd years out at Penrith. The house is paid off, the wife and I are comfortable enough, but we've got four grandkids now and I'd like to leave them a little something. Help with uni or a first car, that sort of thing.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Congratulations on the retirement, that's a big milestone. And that's a lovely reason to look into it. Do you have any existing life cover, maybe through your super?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: I did through my super, but it dropped off when I stopped working, as far as I can tell. So nothing at the moment.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Okay, thanks. And roughly what sort of amount were you thinking you'd like to leave?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: I hadn't really pinned it down. Maybe twenty-five thousand each? So a hundred thousand all up, if that's not silly money.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Not silly at all. Our cover goes from fifty thousand up to a million dollars, so a hundred thousand sits comfortably in that range. I should mention that anything I tell you today is general advice only, and it doesn't take into account your personal objectives, financial situation or needs, so it's worth thinking about whether it suits you.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Righto, understood. Do I need to go and see a doctor or anything? I'm not mad about needles.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: No medical exam at all. Acceptance is based on a few health questions I'd ask you over the phone.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Oh good. What's the catch, then? There's always a catch.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Fair question. There are two main things to know. First, in the first twelve months of the policy, only accidental death is covered. So if you passed away from an illness in that first year, it wouldn't pay out. After twelve months, you're covered more broadly.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Hm. Okay. And the second?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: The premiums are stepped. That means they go up each year as you get older, so what you pay now won't stay the same. It'll increase every year.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Every year? By how much?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: It depends on your age each year, so it rises gradually as you get older. The increase would be shown on your renewal notice each year before it kicks in, so you'd always know in advance.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: I see. That's something to think about on a pension. Well, let's see what it'd cost to begin with.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Sure. I'll just run through the health questions. In the last five years, have you been diagnosed with or treated for cancer, heart disease or a stroke?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No, none of those.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Are you currently waiting on any tests, or have you been advised to have any tests or surgery that haven't happened yet?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No. I've got a bit of high blood pressure, but it's managed with tablets. The GP's happy with it.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thanks for mentioning that. Managed blood pressure is fine for our purposes. And have you smoked any tobacco in the last twelve months?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Gave up in 1994. Haven't touched one since.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Good on you. Alright, based on those answers, for one hundred thousand dollars of cover, your starting premium would be seventy-four dollars a month.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Seventy-four. And that goes up each year, like you said.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That's right, it's stepped, so it'll increase each year as you get older.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Hm. I'm not sure. I'd sort of want to talk to Margaret about it. She handles the budget, really.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That's completely fine, Liam. There's no rush at all. You're welcome to talk it over with her and call back whenever suits you, and the quote's based on your answers, so we can always run it again.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: What happens if I sign up and then change my mind?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: You'd have a thirty-day cooling-off period. If you cancel within those thirty days, you get a full refund of anything you've paid.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Right. Well, that's something. I suppose if Marg hates it I can always cancel.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: You could, yes. It's entirely up to you whether you go ahead today or have a think first. Would you like me to set it up now?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Uh... I guess so.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Lovely. I'll just need your payment details. Will that be a bank account or a card?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Bank account, I suppose. Hang on, let me get the card out of my wallet for the numbers. Okay, BSB is 062-118, account number 1047 3392.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thank you. That's BSB 062-118, account 1047 3392, in the name of Liam Patrick O'Brien?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: That's the one. Joint with Margaret, actually, but my name's on it.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: No problem. And the best address for your policy documents?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: 27 Banksia Crescent, Glenmore Park, New South Wales, 2745.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Perfect. That's all done, Liam. Your policy's now active, and your documents will be posted out to you in the next few days, with an email copy too if we have your address on file.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Oh. Right, that was quick. I'll keep an eye out for them, then.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Is there anything else I can help you with today?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No, I think that's it. I'd better go and tell Margaret what I've done.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Ha, good luck. Thanks so much for calling, Liam, and enjoy the retirement. Have a lovely day.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: You too, Mia. Ta-ta.
